done.why: The lizard door wanted some specific food I never found, and the glacier needed dragon heat. I had fed it a lot of junk and ran out of ideas.

about: A Zork II style underground empire. A wizard teases you while you hunt the treasures he took, which sit south of a ravine. There is a garden, a spinning carousel room, an ice room, and a lizard-guarded door.

moments.note: The Wizard gave a spoken hint about where the treasures were, and said my hands held nothing he valued.
Reading the Zork I copy that the Wizard's word had conjured: the room apologised for it, then settled down.
The Wizard cast Fear on me and I scrambled away.
The carousel scrambled my directions, but the narration explained it and gave hints.
The glacier needs something's mouth heat, which is a good hint.
I fed the lizard four items and none was right. I had no clue what it wanted.

wished: Examine the lizard or get a hint about what it eats
Find the stone door with the question and the pearls
Find the dragon heat for the ice

lines.line: His eye goes to your hands, which hold nothing he values, and he relaxes a little
lines.why: The Wizard's look doubled as a hint about where the treasure was.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Funny, and it fit the Wizard's spells.

lines.line: exactly as hungry as before. That was not what it wanted
lines.why: A clear, witty failure message that told me to try something else.

engagement.why: The Wizard's random visits kept things lively.

difficulty.why: Puzzles are fair but I was left without clues about the lizard.

interestingness.why: A Zork II remix with new Wizard-spell wrinkles.

prose.why: Witty narration added to the classic text.
